title: Disagreement with Delaunay over modern jazz
summary: He recounts Delaunay playing Gillespie and Parker and objects to dissonance without resolution, citing his teacher.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: It's an instrument I love to play. You say you have some of these in your collection. Yeah. Oh, go ahead, Frank, and give me some of your opinions on the... All broad generalizations on the status of jazz now and...

Well, my opinion... I told Dolaunay in Paris, when he brought in those records from Gillespie over, he called me up and told me to come up and listen to him. Yeah. And I spent about two hours at the hot club of Paris, which he called himself the President of... Yeah. And I listened to it. I didn't say nothing. So when he finished, I asked him who was Gillespie. He said, well, he's a modern musician, and Charlie Parker. I didn't know about those two guys. Yeah. He also mentioned Stan Kenton. And that was the future music, what he told me. My answer to him was, as long as you... Those bands going to exist, like Charlie Parker's playing, like Gillespie's playing, and Stan Kenton, I'll never be out of job. That was my answer to him. Yeah. And he laughed at me. He says, you don't... He told me I didn't know what I was talking about. Well, I studied music. Yeah. I studied from Julian Farnes. His name is... Which... He's one of the greatest teachers in Paris, and I would say in France. And if it comes to a push, I think it would be one of the best in Europe, anyway.

And I had to spend, at that time, about six years studying with him. I knew what he taught me of harmony. And when I heard the harmonization of those bands, and this crazy resolution, which didn't exist because everything was dissonant and artificial.

And I said, I studied music. I don't understand it. I have analyzed Chowdhysky's music with my teacher. I have analyzed Chowdhysky's music, Beethoven's music, and Bach, which is the master of harmony.
When I heard what they was doing, and I thought of what Bach had done a hundred years before, but he had resolution with his dissonance.
And retard, as they call it in French. That's right. They had somewhere they wanted to go with it. They had relaxation. He relaxed. He brought in all kinds of dissonance, no, to a resolution.

Wherein those guys, they came up with a whole other dissonance of all kinds and no resolution. They begin with whatever the name of the chord they give, those chords, and end up with something that you don't hear the fundamental note. Everything, and you can't end up on a tonic, and you can't end up on a sixth, you can't end up on the ninth. That's what they told me, because I didn't lose no time analyzing it. Is that photographing? See, I didn't lose no time analyzing it. So.
